sections.topic: Reservation · Backward Classes in the Constitution
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-5 › Reservation - constitutional basis, Indra Sawhney, creamy layer, EWS reservation, promotion in reservation › Backward Classes in the Constitution
bullets: "Backward Classes" is not defined in the Constitution (APPSC G2 2017 key: the "defined" statement is the wrong one).

27% OBC quota in central jobs from 1993; in central educational institutions under the CEI (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006, in force Jan 2007 (IYB 2026 says 2007) after the 2005 amendment to Art. 15 (IYB) [GK for the Act's year].
NCBC: constitutional body under Art. 338B, examines inclusion/exclusion requests (APPCA Apr 2026).

Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006 (in force 2007): 27% OBC seats in central institutions (IYB; GS 2007 key: 93rd Amendment); OBC = classes "so determined by the Central Government" (APP).

sections.topic: Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-3 › National Commission for SCs (338), STs (338A) and Backward Classes (338B); Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities (350B) › Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC
bullets: *Indra Sawhney v UoI* (16 Nov 1992) upheld 27% OBC reservation, introduced the creamy layer, and directed a permanent body for OBC-list inclusion/exclusion → NCBC Act, 1993 (in force 2 April 1993).
102nd Amendment Act, 2018 inserted Art. 338B - NCBC became constitutional; composition: Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and 3 members appointed by the President; civil court powers.
The 102nd Amendment also removed backward classes from the NCSC's purview .
105th Amendment, 2021 restored the States' power to prepare their own SEBC lists (after the Maratha quota judgment) .

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-1 › Right to Equality - Articles 14-18; reasonable classification, reservation jurisprudence › Reservation cases - ruling issue, creamy layer and 50% ceiling origin
bullets: M.R. Balaji: Year 1963; Ruling Reservation should generally stay below 50%
Indra Sawhney: Year 1992; Ruling 27% OBC quota upheld; creamy layer excluded; 50% ceiling; no reservation in promotions [GK for last two]
Indra Sawhney (16 Nov 1992): Issue decided 9-judge bench, 6:3: 27% OBC quota valid with creamy layer out; 50% cap; no reservation in promotion (UPSC; IYB)

Maratha case (Jaishri Patil, 2021): Issue decided Maratha quota struck down for crossing 50% without exceptional circumstances; read the 102nd Amendment as making the Central list the only SEBC list (UPSC)
M.R. Balaji v State of Mysore (1962): Held Caste cannot be the sole test; reservation must be reasonable, below 50% (APP's case table dates it 1960)

sections.topic: Transgender persons · Reservation and state measures

items.title: DDWS Organizes Second Follow-up Meeting to accelerate drinking water coverage in tribal areas under PM-JANMAN and DA-JGUA
items.summary: The meeting was chaired by the Secretary, DDWS and attended by senior officials of the National Jal Jeevan Mission (NJJM), Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA), State Rural Water Supply/Public Health Engineering Departments, State Tribal Welfare Departments and other concerned stakeholders.

facts.text: The meeting was chaired by the Secretary, DDWS and attended by senior officials of the National Jal Jeevan Mission (NJJM), Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA), State Rural Water Supply/Public Health Engineering Departments, State Tribal Welfare Departments and other concerned stakeholders.

The meeting was held as part of the follow-up process initiated after the Departmental Summit, where States and Union Territories had committed to achieving saturation of drinking water coverage in all eligible PM-JANMAN and DA-JGUA villages.
A dedicated provision of ₹5,000 crore under JJM 2.0 has been earmarked to address drinking water gaps in PM-JANMAN and DA-JGUA villages.

Any discrepancies identified during the exercise are to be resolved through consultation and field verification, wherever required, so that a final validated database is available at the district level.

sections.topic: PESA Act 1996; Fifth and Sixth Schedule areas and tribal self-governance
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-3 › PESA Act 1996; Fifth and Sixth Schedule areas and tribal self-governance › PESA Act 1996 - committee, states, Gram Sabha powers
bullets: Needed because Art. 243M excludes Scheduled and tribal areas from Part IX. Art. 243M(4)(b) lets Parliament extend it, and such a law is not an amendment under Art. 368.

Gram Sabha (at para/majra/tola level) and Panchayats get powers over: intoxicants; ownership of minor forest produce; preventing tribal land alienation and restoring unlawfully alienated land; village markets; money-lending to STs; social-sector institutions; local plans and tribal sub-plans.

Higher-level panchayats must not usurp Gram Sabha powers. States should follow the Sixth Schedule pattern for district-level (Zila Panchayat) arrangements. Inconsistent state laws lapse one year after assent.

Zila Panchayat in Scheduled Areas: plans minor water bodies, controls social-sector institutions and Tribal Sub-Plans, and does other functions conferred by the State (CGPSC 2016 - "all of the above").
Operationalises Art. 243M(4)(b): extends Part IX (Panchayats) to Fifth Schedule Areas with exceptions (VIS 2026, CDX); recognises governance through customary law (VIS).

items.title: Sādhana Śhrinkhla: First Regional Workshop on Mission Karmayogi Concludes at Vijayawada
items.summary: The two-day workshop (29–30 September 2026) was themed " From Training Institutions to Capacity Building Institutions ". It brought together more than 300 participants from Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Telangana, Odisha, Puducherry, Kerala and Tamil Nadu, along with Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) from these States/UTs.

facts.text: It builds on the stakeholder consultations organized by CBC previously, like - National Training Conclave during Sādhana Saptah 2026 (2–8 April 2026), which focused on Technology, Tradition and Tangible Outcomes, and the National Departmental Summit on "Institutionalizing Capacity Building: From …

He welcomed UNNATI for connecting National, Regional and State Training Institutions on one platform, and suggested extending the network to universities and the private sector so that officials gain first-hand exposure to different working environments.

Day 1: Technical sessions Transformation from Training Institution to Capacity Building Institution: The first session, anchored through UNNATI, explained how TIs can move from delivering individual programmes to managing the complete capacity-building lifecycle.
All the participating State/UT’s also presented their progress on related Mission Karmayogi parameters.

items.title: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Participates in Opening Day of G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting in Milwauke, U.S
items.summary: Speaking at the session on food and trade, Shri Goyal thanked the Presidency for placing food at the centre of the discussions. He said that ensuring food security for all and creating greater opportunities for farmers are central to India’s policy and reiterated that food must never be used as an instrument of pressure against any country.

facts.text: Shri Goyal said that during the COVID-19 pandemic, India ensured food security for over 1.4 billion citizens and supplied foodgrains to several countries in need.
He noted that over 800 million people in India are currently being provided foodgrains free of cost.

Shri Goyal also referred to existing mechanisms, including the G20 Agricultural Market Information System, established in 2011, and the exemption of purchases by the World Food Programme from export restrictions, adopted at the 12th Ministerial Conference of the WTO.
The Minister also attended the welcome dinner hosted by Ambassador Greer and Secretary Rollins of the United States Department of Agriculture at the Milwaukee Art Museum.

items.title: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code has strengthened credit discipline, improved recovery climate and contributed to ease of doing business: Harsh Malhotra, MoS, Corporate Affairs Ministry
items.summary: Chief guest Shri Harsh Malhotra in his inaugural address, observed that the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC) has strengthened credit discipline, improved the recovery climate and contributed to the ease of doing business in the country.

facts.text: He highlighted that the IBC has seen seven sets of amendments to the Code in the last ten years.
While noting the positive outcomes of IBC, he emphasised the need for timelines to be respected by all stakeholders.

Shri Ansuman Pattnaik, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, while noting the achievements of the IBC, highlighted the policy reforms undertaken to strengthen the Code, including the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (Amendment) Act, 2026.

He observed that the ecosystem now comprises over 4,400 Insolvency Professionals and over 6,000 Registered Valuers, highlighting the responsive, participative and evidence-based approach to regulation-making being adopted by IBBI.

bullets: Insolvency is a financial state: being unable to pay debts as they fall due. Bankruptcy is the legal declaration that follows (BPSC 2023 key: the two statements reversing these are wrong) .

IBC Amendment Act 2026: NCLT must admit or reject a CIRP plea within 14 days. It adds a Creditor-Initiated Insolvency Resolution Process (CIIRP), a hybrid of debtor-in-possession and creditor-in-control, plus an out-of-court route (LENS Jun 2026; TH 31 Mar and 15 Jun 2026).

Insolvency = the *state* of being unable to pay debts when due; bankruptcy = the *legal* declaration/process for an insolvent individual or firm . BPSC 2023 swapped the two definitions, making those statements false.

items.title: Union Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas Shri Hardeep Singh Puri launches GOBARdhan Scheme to accelerate development of India’s Compressed Biogas sector
items.summary: The Scheme, approved by the Union Cabinet on 6 August 2026 with an outlay of ₹23,731 crore, provides a ten-year framework from FY 2026–27 to FY 2035–36 for accelerating CBG development in India. The scheme aims to increase domestic CBG production nearly 10-fold (to around 5 MMSCMD) with a long-term framework that gives investors and lenders greater certainty.

facts.text: The Scheme, approved by the Union Cabinet on 6 August 2026 with an outlay of ₹23,731 crore, provides a ten-year framework from FY 2026–27 to FY 2035–36 for accelerating CBG development in India.

The procurement obligation has been prescribed at 3% in FY 2026–27, 4% in FY 2027–28 and 5% from FY 2028–29 onwards for the CNG (Transport) and PNG (Domestic) segment The Scheme introduces an administered CBG price of ₹2,110 per MMBtu, providing greater revenue visibility to producers.

Eligible greenfield projects can receive capital assistance of up to ₹2 crore per TPD of installed CBG capacity, including support for plant machinery, feedstock aggregation and FOM/LFOM processing and manure value-addition equipment.
The guarantee cap is ₹20 crore per project for general MSME projects and ₹25 crore per project for women-led MSME projects, providing enhanced support to women entrepreneurs in the CBG sector.

Not against private individuals/bodies; not for discretionary functions or legislative functions.

items.title: From AI to EVs: How Technology Is Transforming Urban Swachhata
items.summary: 01 OCT 2026 1:01PM by PIB Delhi On October 2, 2014, the Swachh Bharat Mission began with a simple idea: keep our surroundings clean. Avoid littering public spaces and make cleanliness a shared responsibility. What began with brooms, bins and citizen participation soon became a mass movement. Today, that movement is embracing a new generation of technology.

facts.text: The initiative eliminates the need for more than 71,000 litres of diesel annually and is estimated to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 21,000 tonnes over a decade.
The vehicles travel around 40 km a day, replacing diesel-powered collection vehicles with e-rickshaws and helping reduce pollution.
The fleet reduces around 41 tonnes of carbon emissions each day, amounting to an annual reduction of 15,160 tonnes.
The fleet now covers 24,621 streets and more than 2.1 million households, while audio systems on the vehicles carry waste-segregation messages through neighbourhoods.

facts.text: The participants shared first-hand experiences of restoring rivers and ponds, undertaking Shramdaan, promoting rainwater harvesting, removing plastic and other waste near water bodies, carrying out plantation drives and mobilising women, youth, volunteers and local communities.

bullets: A wet-bulb temperature of about 35°C is the limit of human survivability, because above it sweat can no longer cool the body . The World Bank warned that India could be among the first places to cross it routinely (UPSC 2025).
A CMIP6 study finds around 40 coastal districts could warm by more than 1°C by 2040. Kerala and Tamil Nadu could see wet-bulb temperatures of about 31°C (LENSD 7 Jun 2026).
Heat Action Plans: Ahmedabad drew up the first one in South Asia, in 2013 .

The Dasra report "Under the Weather" finds that nearly 40% of districts face high risk from extreme weather. Warmer, wetter conditions are expanding dengue and malaria, floods bring cholera and hepatitis, and heat brings heatstroke and cardiovascular strain (TH 10 Apr 2026). Urban waterlogging, as in Mumbai, spreads leptospirosis, typhoid and hepatitis A (TH 7 Apr 2026).

The opening of 1 million sq km of previously restricted sedimentary basins has helped in boosting domestic hydrocarbon exploration and gas availability.

items.title: Dr. Virendra Kumar, Shri B L Verma To Distribute Assistive Devices Among Senior Citizens On Swachh Bharat Diwas Tomorrow
items.summary: Verma, Hon’ble Minister of State of Social Justice and Empowerment, will also grace the occasion. A Senior Official in the Ministry informed that under the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY), 114 senior citizens residing in Senior Citizens’ Homes in New Delhi and the National Capital Region will receive a total of 662 assistive devices and aids costing over ₹10 lakh, free of cost.

facts.text: A Senior Official in the Ministry informed that under the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY), 114 senior citizens residing in Senior Citizens’ Homes in New Delhi and the National Capital Region will receive a total of 662 assistive devices and aids costing over ₹10 lakh, free of cost.

The assistive devices include folding wheelchairs and commode wheelchairs, crutches, walking sticks, BTE hearing aids, spinal supports, walkers, cervical collars, chairs with commode, knee braces, LS belts, tripods/tetrapods and silicone foam cushions.

The Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana, launched on 1st April 2017, is fully funded by the Government of India and provides free assistive devices to eligible senior citizens with age-related physical frailty.
Since its launch, more than 55 lakh assistive devices have been provided to more than 10 lakh senior citizens across the country, with about 45 per cent of the beneficiaries being women.

items.title: PM E-DRIVE Scheme
items.summary: 01 OCT 2026 7:17PM by PIB Delhi Electric mobility is gathering pace, driven by targeted policies, financial incentives and supportive measures. At the centre of this shift is the PM E-DRIVE Scheme, launched in September 2024. It aims to accelerate EV adoption, expand charging infrastructure and strengthen the domestic EV manufacturing ecosystem.

facts.text: At the centre of this shift is the PM E-DRIVE Scheme, launched in September 2024.
With an outlay of ₹11,900 crore and implementation extended until March 2028, the scheme supports multiple EV categories and infrastructure.
It supports incentives for ~28.30 lakh EVs and has enabled 26.59 lakh sales as of June 2026.
Originally notified for a two-year period, the Scheme has been extended to 31 March 2028 .

items.title: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan calls for making cleanliness a part of everyday public behaviour, not limiting it to campaigns
items.summary: Addressing a virtual meeting with the Secretaries and senior officials of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and the Ministry of Rural Development, he called for active participation by officials and employees in cleanliness activities and urged them to lead by example.

facts.text: He placed particular emphasis on effectively connecting rural areas, panchayats and field-level offices with cleanliness activities and ensuring the participation of farmers, rural communities, sanitation workers, the media and other relevant stakeholders.

These included cleanliness pledges, Swachh Pathshala activities, participation of young people, solid waste management, cleanliness drives across office premises, and intensive cleaning of corridors, canteens and toilets at headquarters and field offices.
It was informed during the meeting that the disposal and auction of old furniture and electronic waste had generated revenue of approximately Rs 15 lakh .

Regarding the Special Campaign to be conducted from October 2 to October 31, 2026 , all departments shared details of the targets set for the disposal of pending files and cases, reduction in the number of pending matters, disposal of scrap and e-waste, better utilisation of office space and remo…

bullets: Private bank entry (HDFC, ICICI), later FDI up to 74% in private banks (2004) (CDI; APP).
RBI made the primary regulator, ending dual control with the Finance Ministry's Banking Division; PSB autonomy (UPSC).

Belong: deregulation of interest rates (APPSC GS 2023 key), cuts in SLR/CRR, prudential norms (CRAR 1992, income recognition, asset classification, provisioning), private bank entry (HDFC, ICICI; by 1995), statutory SEBI (1992), market-determined exchange rate (1993), FERA replaced by FEMA (1999), insurance opened by the IRDA Act 1999. Do not belong: bank nationalisation (1969/1980, pre-reform); the FRBM Act 2003, which is a *fiscal* reform, not financial-sector.

bullets: Surplus liquidity speeds up transmission and pulls market rates below the repo. Deficit liquidity weakens it.

bullets: Constituted 18 November 2004 (answer to "which year": 2004), chaired by Prof. M.S. Swaminathan; set up to address the calamity of farmer suicides; submitted five reports (2004-06) .

An operational holding is all land used for agricultural production and operated as one technical unit by one person, alone or with others, regardless of title, size or location.

bullets: "Backward Classes" is not defined in the Constitution (APPSC G2 2017 key: the "defined" statement is the wrong one).

27% OBC quota in central jobs from 1993; in central educational institutions under the CEI (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006, in force Jan 2007 (IYB 2026 says 2007) after the 2005 amendment to Art. 15 (IYB) [GK for the Act's year].

Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006 (in force 2007): 27% OBC seats in central institutions (IYB; GS 2007 key: 93rd Amendment); OBC = classes "so determined by the Central Government" (APP).

sections.topic: Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-3 › National Commission for SCs (338), STs (338A) and Backward Classes (338B); Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities (350B) › Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC
bullets: *Indra Sawhney v UoI* (16 Nov 1992) upheld 27% OBC reservation, introduced the creamy layer, and directed a permanent body for OBC-list inclusion/exclusion → NCBC Act, 1993 (in force 2 April 1993).
The 102nd Amendment also removed backward classes from the NCSC's purview .

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-4 › Social stratification and mobility in India › Mobility through reservation, education, migration
bullets: Education: better education brings better jobs and higher social standing; the emerging class system allows upward mobility (APP).
Reservation: backward classes in the South (Self-Respect Movement of Periyar) demanded reservation in government jobs; reservation led to group mobility (APP).
Reservation has also broadened the urban middle class by bringing in backward classes and Dalits (APP).
Occupational mobility: e.g., Ezhavas of Kerala moved from toddy tapping into tailoring and cottage industries (APP).
Migration and urbanisation: city anonymity and caste-blind public spaces weaken caste identity, but migrants carry caste networks and prejudices into cities (APP).

bullets: Debate: NALSA (2014) asked governments to treat transgender persons as socially and educationally backward (a vertical OBC-type quota); the community seeks horizontal reservation cutting across SC/ST/OBC/General. The issue resurfaced in June 2023 with a Mumbai protest against Maharashtra's reply to the Bombay High Court (APPSC 2022).
Karnataka - first State to give 1% reservation to transgender persons in all government services (July 2021) (APPSC 2023).

items.title: FIEO to organise One-Day Program on Customs Schemes for Exporters in Hyderabad
items.summary: 01 OCT 2026 10:20AM by PIB Hyderabad Federation of Indian Export Organisations (FIEO) is organising a one-day program on “Customs Schemes for Exporters: Benefits, Procedures and Compliances” on 9th October 2026 (Friday) at Hyderabad in association with ICICI Bank.

facts.text: The program is aimed at creating awareness among exporters, manufacturers, MSMEs and trade stakeholders about key Customs schemes and facilitation measures available for international trade, with particular emphasis on benefits, eligibility, procedures, documentation and compliance requirements.

The program will cover a range of important topics, including: Overview of Customs Facilitation for Exporters, including the role of Customs in export promotion, ICEGATE and electronic Customs procedures, Risk Management System and faceless assessment.
Customs Compliance for Exporters, including Shipping Bill and supporting documents, classification and valuation, country-of-origin requirements, record keeping, audit, common errors and penalties.

FIEO provides a wide range of services to exporters, including market research, trade information, export promotion activities, organizing overseas trade fairs and exhibitions, training programs, and policy advocacy.

bullets: It merges 9 laws (EPF, ESI, Maternity Benefit, Gratuity, Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act, etc.). The four Labour Codes came into force on 21 Nov 2025, with the 2026 Central Rules (CDI Block15).

AP angle: Kadapa-Kurnool limestone makes Rayalaseema a cement hub; the Eastern Ghats hold bauxite, but mining there must respect tribal areas and biodiversity.

Unapportioned debt: more than Rs 24,000 crore of public debt is still on AP's books, which eats into its FRBM borrowing room (CDI Block04).
